1. Exact text the user supplied, or explicit agreement earlier in the conversation, counts as agreement.
2. A general request to make the change does not count as agreement.

This sentence covers both parts.
- The sentence appears in the gate for agreement on the requirement groups, so "agreement" has its intended meaning there.
- "Build the feature" and "make the change" mean the same thing here, so the different wording is not a gap.
- The skill states nothing else about what counts as agreement, so there is no unspecified behavior.

I did not read `collapse`. I assumed it normalizes whitespace, because the sentence wraps across lines in `SKILL.md`. The test would fail if the sentence were missing or changed. It covers both parts of the obligation because both are in the one asserted sentence.

I found no gaps.
